description: run.sh's generate_draft real-content hook only checks `[ -n "${ARTICLE_REAL_DRAFT_PATH:-}" ] && [ -f "${ARTICLE_REAL_DRAFT_PATH:-}" ]` to decide between state (a) (real content, verbatim) and state (b) (boilerplate safety-net). This means a caller that SUPPLIES a real ARTICLE_REAL_DRAFT_PATH pointing at a NON-EXISTENT file (e.g. a typo, a race condition where the file hasn't been written yet, or a wiring bug in the real daily-executor) silently falls through to the SAME undocumented boilerplate branch as state (b) -- with ZERO stderr diagnostic anywhere distinguishing 'caller never intended a real draft' from 'caller intended a real draft but the path was wrong'. Neither PROP-19's row in verification-architecture.md nor CRIT-103's passThreshold acknowledges this 'path supplied but missing' sub-case as a distinct, intentional state, and no test in tests/test-prop19-real-content-hook.sh exercises it. In the real REQ-19 daily-executor path (which per the spec always supplies topic/research and the draft together), a wiring bug of this exact shape would cause the wake to silently draft/publish Sprint-1 boilerplate content under Mode A instead of the agent's real researched article, completely undetected, defeating PROP-19's entire purpose.

evidence.snippet:
generate_draft() {
  local topic="$1" out="$2"
  if [ "${ARTICLE_TEST:-}" != "1" ] && [ -n "${ARTICLE_REAL_DRAFT_PATH:-}" ] && [ -f "${ARTICLE_REAL_DRAFT_PATH:-}" ]; then
    cp "$ARTICLE_REAL_DRAFT_PATH" "$out"
    return 0
  fi
  cat > "$out" <<EOF
# ${topic}: the pattern most people miss in the first 10 hours
...
